#ggplot2 is an R package used to create attractive and professional data visualizations.
#install ggplot2 packages
install.packages("ggplot2")
#load ggplot2
library(ggplot2)
#view top six cars data
head(cars)
#summary of cars data
summary(cars)
#create scatter plot
ggplot(data=cars,aes(x=dist, y=speed)) + geom_point()
#create histogram graph
ggplot(data=cars, aes(x=speed)) +geom_histogram(binwidth=1)
ggplot(data=cars, aes(x=dist)) +geom_histogram(binwidth=1)
# Students dataframe
```{r}
students <- data.frame(
  Name = c("John", "Mary", "Peter", "Alice", "David"),
  Gender = c("Male", "Female", "Male", "Female", "Male"),
  Age = c(22, 21, 24, 23, 25),
  Marks = c(70, 85, 65, 90, 75)
)
print(students)
```
#create bar chart
```{r}
ggplot(data = students,aes(x = Gender, fill = Gender)) +      geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
labs(
 title = "Number of Students Per Gender",
 x = "Gender",
 y = "Number of Students"
) +
theme_classic()
```
#create Histogram
```{r}
ggplot(data = students, aes(x = Marks)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 3)
```
#creating Scatterplot
```{r}
ggplot(data = students, aes(x = Age, y = Marks)) + 
geom_point(
color = "blue",
size = 3,
shape = 16
) + 
geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "black")+
labs(
 title = "Relationship between Age and Marks",
 x = "Student age",
 y = "Student Marks"
) +
theme_classic()
```

# craeting Boxplot
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(data = students, aes(x = Gender, y = Marks)) + 
  geom_boxplot(fill = "skyblue") +
  labs(
   title = "Boxplot of Student Marks",
   x = "Gender",
   y = "Student Marks"
) +
theme_classic()
```
#creating bar chart graph
```{r}
ggplot(students, aes(x = Gender, fill = Gender)) +
  geom_bar(position = "stack")
```
# mortality Data 
```{r}
mortality <- data.frame(
  Month = rep(c("Jan", "Feb", "Mar",
                "Apr", "May", "Jun"), 2),

  Type = rep(c("Community", "Health Facility"), each = 6),

  Deaths = c(
    15, 18, 20, 17, 25, 22,
    10, 12, 11, 14, 13, 16
  )
)
print(mortality)
```
# Create multiple line graphs
```{r}
ggplot(mortality,
       aes(x = Month, y = Deaths,
           color = Type, group = Type)) +

  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +

  geom_point(size = 2) +

  labs(
    title = "Community vs Facility Deaths",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Number of Deaths",
    color = "Death Type"
  ) +

  theme_classic()
```
